name: How can I tell if my older home has already been seismically retrofitted or not?

mainEntity.name: How can I tell if my older home has already been seismically retrofitted or not?

acceptedAnswer.text:
DIRECT ANSWER: You can’t rely on guesswork; you need to look for documentation and physical signs of retrofit work, ideally verified by a professional inspection.

CONTEXT: Many retrofits happen in crawlspaces, garages, and behind finishes, so they’re easy to miss. Conversely, some homes have partial or inadequate retrofits that don’t meet current standards.

KEY FACTORS:
- City permits and inspection records showing foundation bolting or structural work.
- Visible anchor bolts, hold‑downs, and plywood shear walls in crawlspaces or garages.
- Engineering reports or letters from prior owners.
- Age and quality of the work compared with current best practices.

PRACTICAL GUIDANCE: Start by requesting permit history from your local building department, then have a contractor or engineer walk through and verify what was actually done. Ask them to flag any incomplete or outdated previous retrofits.

SOFT POSITIONING: A brief professional assessment can turn “I think it’s retrofitted” into clear, documented facts about your home’s condition.
acceptedAnswer.description: To confirm if your home has been seismically retrofitted, check city permit and inspection records, look in crawlspaces and garages for anchor bolts, hold‑downs, and plywood bracing, and have a qualified pro inspect the work. Many older homes have partial or outdated retrofits that need upgrading.
